title: WP6 maize: crop parameters and Earth check (declared before the check data are read)
parameters: scripts/land_people.py MAIZE (sources in the code comment: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 66 maize chapter, local copy data/cache/maize_sources/fao66_i2800e07.pdf; FAO-33 Ky; USDA kcal). Opt-in only (extra_crops); every default run unchanged (tests pass).
run: scripts/land_people_earth.py --window 7,33,-118,-77 --extra-crops maize (WorldClim 1970-2000, the adopted arable/irrigation rules), Mexico and Central America.
check_data: MapSPAM 2010 v2.0 (Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/PRFF8V), physical area GeoTIFF, maize rain-fed (all rain-fed systems), 5 arc-min; data/cache/mapspam2010 (not redistributed).

tests.T1_rank: Spearman correlation across land cells of the window between the model's maize kcal/ha (rain-fed share as modelled) and MapSPAM rain-fed maize physical area as a share of cell area: pass if >= 0.30.
tests.T2_coverage: Share of MapSPAM rain-fed maize physical area lying in cells where the model's maize kcal/ha > 0: pass if >= 0.80.
tests.T3_season: Median first month of the model's maize season over cells 19-21 N, 101-97 W (central Mexican highlands) with maize > 0: pass if May or June.

outcome_use: Pass: maize enters the New World runs (WP6 next step: New World heartland cores, then the reserved Valley of Mexico blind test, declared separately). Fail: report, and revise only by a declared amendment.
caveat: MapSPAM is modern (2010) land use: it tests where maize can be grown rain-fed, not ancient yields.

result.outcome: PASS (T1 0.42, T2 0.976, T3 June). Caveat: maize is suitable in 95 % of land cells, so T2 is weak; T1 carries the test. With the Old World crops also allowed, maize is the main crop in only 12,748 of 51,365 cells (barley 14,518, millet 11,863, rice 10,116): pre-Columbian New World runs need a New World crop set.
